Improve the supplied frozen Qwen3-8B's reusable legal decision procedures from ACTUAL already-seen OpenExempt TRAIN observations. The actor answers EC and EV directly, with the same public facts, statutes, solved steps and response schema as the strong empty-library control. Its weights never change. It has NO program interpreter or stored numerical routines. All skill operators arrays MUST be empty. Do not tell it to use null, call a routine, write code, or submit a claim plan. Plain-language statutory calculations may be taught where an actual error warrants them, but prioritize observed legal-selection and factual-grounding mistakes. Use only the benchmark statute version and released TRAIN evidence supplied here; no tools, outside law, future cases, test answers or invented successful experience. Compare the actual parent prediction, released target, and same-case controls. Identify the mistaken legal condition or omitted alternative before changing a skill. An extra law, a missing law and a wrong amount require different corrections. The native_claim_feedback identifies these errors with the unchanged original asset/claim matcher and amount tolerance; the original answer, target and scores remain authoritative. Repair an omitted alternative with a public factual trigger, not a circular condition such as 'when already valuing this paragraph'. Retain every independently eligible alternative rather than replacing a specific law with a general-property alternative or vice versa. For valuation repairs, state the final protected amount for the WHOLE named asset. Distinguish a per-debtor statutory ceiling from the asset-level output; do not leave a half-interest as the final answer, or double every ceiling merely because two debtors exist. Attach exclusions to the particular alternative they exclude, not every other applicable alternative for that asset. Derive the legal branches from the supplied statute and TRAIN evidence, not a new universal spouse or allocation rule. Verify the task and supplied statute before treating a cap as an eligibility test. Write short decision instructions: which factual condition to check, which legal alternative it enables, and which exception prevents a false positive. Keep correct unrelated boundaries verbatim; do not rewrite a whole jurisdiction for style, broaden a rule from one case, or add a generic instruction already present. Do not store case IDs, debtors, exact asset names or instance values, answer tables, or copied target sets. A deidentified procedural output illustration is allowed under the execution-teaching contract, not an answer lookup. Public statutory citations and statutory dollar limits may be used where supported by the supplied law. Each skill has id, hypothesis_ids listing its public EC/EV tasks, and guidance. Guidance contains by_task, jurisdiction and an empty operators array. Each declared task has exactly one explicit when/procedure/avoid_when block. Identical task guidance may share one block; different task guidance costs its full stored tokens. Jurisdiction is one supplied legal namespace, or ALL only for genuinely shared procedure. Only the public task and already-given allowable jurisdictions select guidance; they do not supply asset eligibility answers. Publish minimal CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE or MERGE deltas against original parent IDs. Unmentioned skills stay verbatim. UPDATE retains its one target ID; DELETE has one target and null skill; MERGE consumes at least two IDs; CREATE has no target. Do not force library growth. Delete misleading guidance, merge true duplication, or explicitly NOOP if no grounded repair is available. Audit source_case_ids and rationales must reference supplied seen sources and never reach the actor. The body declares the fixed TRAIN commit policy. Under legal_scope, public co-visible namespaces, shared guidance changes and moved IDs couple edits. A coordinate needs current-source evidence. Preserve BOTH native and complete-output mean F1 on the current cohort and on ALL already-seen sources, separately per task. On the prior cohort each mean may decrease by at most 0.01, one percentage point, relative to its actual parent. Require strict current improvement. Invalid answers still score zero and complete-output F1 still penalizes every false claim, including negative or unmatched assets. Report all format and false-claim counts, but their individual counts are diagnostics, not additional absolute zero-increase vetoes. The all-seen constraint must also hold for the final actual composed library. Native EC can hide false citations on assets with no applicable law; never call those safe. Other declared policies assess entire tasks or the whole proposal instead. Under adaptive_legal, a globally admissible complete proposal and an admissible dependency-composed proposal are compared using their already observed seen-TRAIN replays. Prefer the larger minimum EC/EV complete-output-F1 gain, then the larger mean gain; exact ties retain the complete proposal. A complete proposal need not pass every smaller context's gate. No extra answer generation or changed scorer is used. The final single composed library must still pass the full TRAIN gate. Replay uses ALL seen sources, not just the communication subset, and is training optimization, not validation or proof of generalization. No answer repair, extra inference model, per-case answer selection, or changed scorer is allowed. Respect the actual target-tokenizer cap and combination headroom in the body. Keep edits concise enough that accepted components and unchanged guidance fit together. Bounded emitted excerpts are unverified executor output, not verified causal explanations; check them against facts, law, target and actual feedback. Return only the exact delta JSON schema. Diagnose the reusable instruction's operational adequacy, not just whether its legal sentences are true. SKILL_DEFECT includes missing or wrong knowledge, underspecified eligibility, unavailable prerequisites, circular triggers, overloaded rule units and an ineffective representation of otherwise true law. Repeated omissions across supplied sources, or the same failure after an existing reminder, require reconsidering the instruction itself; do not call them isolated EXECUTION_LAPSE merely because a legal sentence is correct. Use actual_actor_skill_messages and their context references to inspect exactly what this task sees. EC and EV do not share their skill blocks or model answers. EV must decide eligibility as well as amounts from its own supplied inputs; do not assume its EC classification has already been solved unless it literally appears in the supplied public solved steps. Every task block must be usable with those inputs alone. A circular instruction such as 'for an eligible law' does not teach the missing eligibility condition. For SKILL_DEFECT, rewrite or reorganize the relevant when/procedure/avoid_when text and use the normal CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE edits as needed. Separate independent decisions when one overloaded block hides them, without a fixed number of skills. Preserve supported legal conditions, exclusions and numeric semantics, but do not freeze an inadequate wording just because it contains a true rule. Do not import another method's library or add case-specific answers. Reserve EXECUTION_LAPSE for an isolated slip supported by the actual comparable success/failure observations; a quoted sentence alone does not establish that the instruction is complete. Quote its current rule anchor. Return delta and diagnoses. Each changed (skill_id, task) projection needs exactly one diagnosis, including created and deleted projections. Its source_case_ids are already supplied TRAIN sources. SKILL_DEFECT may use the normal differential edits. For every newly created (skill_id, task) projection, including a split or a MERGE into a new ID, use an empty rule_anchor: the new ID has no old projection to quote. For an existing projection, a nonempty anchor must quote that same ID/task's actual parent text. An empty anchor for an existing projection denotes a genuinely missing rule, not permission to invent evidence. For EXECUTION_LAPSE, keep the skill ID, task, jurisdiction, operators, when and avoid_when unchanged. Preserve the entire knowledge procedure before the exact delimiter '\nExecution example:'. Append or replace only its compact teaching example after that delimiter. Keep at most one example section per block; update or deduplicate it rather than accumulating reminders. The exact anchor must occur in that block's existing knowledge, not an invented paraphrase. Use concrete final-output behavior, not a synonym of the existing rule: show coexisting independently applicable citations in an asset's JSON, or binding the protected amount to the asset's value instead of blindly copying a cap. Only teach conditions supported by the supplied law and actual TRAIN evidence. Public native final submissions show the actor's actual output representation; they are not automatically successful examples. Deidentify instances and do not save whole training answers. Mark any hypothetical numerical illustration as hypothetical, never as a new verified successful experience. Future assets still require their own eligibility and numeric decisions. No output repair, extra inference call, routing layer, program, or fallback is introduced. All text and examples share the original complete-library token cap. Empty delta and diagnoses are valid when no reusable change is warranted.  This call teaches only the public task declared by teaching_task. The other task is an independent actor, not a prerequisite already solved for this one. Change only the declared task's rendered guidance; the other task's complete projection must remain byte-identical, including skill IDs and jurisdiction. An existing EC-only skill may gain an EV block without changing its EC block, and a shared block may be split to preserve the unselected task verbatim. CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE and MERGE remain available within that boundary; do not force a skill count or one skill per jurisdiction. Separate independently triggered decisions when bundling them hides a reusable action. Use this task's actual answers and released targets to repair its own missing eligibility, co-applicable alternatives or amount computation. Resolve invariant conditions under the declared independent-alternative task before leaving a calculation conditional on an unavailable prerequisite. Do not rewrite the other task to make the library look symmetric. NOOP is valid; the other scheduled task will still be taught. This is one bounded coordinate update, not a quality retry. Candidate feedback retains at most the latest unsuccessful or partially committed historical proposal per teaching task, each with at most eight real TRAIN witnesses. Its accepted flag and origin describe the original decision. Historical candidate outputs were generated under their recorded proposed bank; they are NOT a new replay from the current parent. Current-parent reference answers are separately supplied in already_seen_training. Compare these actual observations without inventing an old parent or a fresh rerun. A NOOP or an unrelated successful edit does not erase the last failure. Target only IDs in this attempt's actual parent, never IDs created earlier in the same delta. Keep committed changes and correct remaining defects using the declared full TRAIN admission contract. This is bounded training feedback, not an inference retry or access to future cases.
EV revision policy: first localize each observed defect to (1) an absent or incorrect eligibility condition, (2) an absent independently applicable alternative, or (3) the value attached to an already correctly selected alternative. Use the smallest instruction edit that corrects the demonstrated decision. For (3), keep the existing eligibility catalogue and exclusions verbatim; edit only the faulty amount-binding clause. Make that clause bind the public debtor/ownership condition, the particular statutory ceiling and the WHOLE named asset value to the SAME citation. Do not transfer a ceiling or debtor multiplier from a different citation or jurisdiction. Preserve correct sibling alternatives and their distinct amounts. For (1) or (2), change only the evidenced condition or add the absent alternative; do not regenerate the whole jurisdiction. A genuinely absent task projection may be created normally. Repeated errors warrant a clearer local representation, not a wholesale rewrite of otherwise supported boundaries. In rejected candidate feedback, inspect losses of previously correct alternatives and changed amounts in unchanged co-visible guidance before repeating that proposal. Keep all correct unrelated when/procedure/avoid_when text verbatim. Do not use instance IDs, facts or amounts in runtime guidance.

United States Code Title 11 - Bankruptcy
11 U.S.C. § 522(b)
(1) An individual debtor may exempt from property of the estate the property listed in either paragraph (2) or, in the alternative, paragraph (3) of this subsection. In joint cases, one debtor may not elect to exempt property listed in paragraph (2) and the other debtor elect to exempt property listed in paragraph (3) of this subsection.
(2) Property listed in this paragraph is property that is specified under subsection (d), unless the State law that is applicable to the debtor under paragraph (3)(A) specifically does not so authorize.
(3) Property listed in this paragraph is- (A) any property that is exempt under State or local law that is applicable on the date of the filing of the petition to the place in which the debtor's domicile has been located for the 730 days immediately preceding the date of the filing of the petition or if the debtor's domicile has not been located in a single State for such 730-day period, the place in which the debtor's domicile was located for 180 days immediately preceding the 730-day period or for a longer portion of such 180-day period than in any other place;

11 U.S.C. § 522(d)
The following property may be exempted under subsection (b)(2) of this section:

11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(1)
The debtor's aggregate interest, not to exceed $27,900 in value, in real property or personal property that the debtor or a dependent of the debtor uses as a residence, in a cooperative that owns property that the debtor or a dependent of the debtor uses as a residence, or in a burial plot for the debtor or a dependent of the debtor.

11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(2)
The debtor's interest, not to exceed $4,450 in value, in one motor vehicle.

11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(3)
The debtor's interest, not to exceed $700 in value in any particular item or $14,875 in aggregate value, in household furnishings, household goods, wearing apparel, appliances, books, animals, crops, or musical instruments, that are held primarily for the personal, family, or household use of the debtor or a dependent of the debtor.

11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(4)
The debtor's aggregate interest, not to exceed $1,875 in value, in jewelry held primarily for the personal, family, or household use of the debtor or a dependent of the debtor.

11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(5)
The debtor's aggregate interest in any property, not to exceed in value $1,475 plus up to $13,950 of any unused amount of the exemption provided under paragraph (1) of this subsection.

11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(6)
The debtor's aggregate interest, not to exceed $2,800 in value, in any implements, professional books, or tools, of the trade of the debtor or the trade of a dependent of the debtor.

11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(9)
Professionally prescribed health aids for the debtor or a dependent of the debtor.

11 U.S.C. § 522(m)
Subject to the limitation in subsection (b), this section shall apply separately with respect to each debtor in a joint case.

Arizona Revised Statutes
Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1101(A)
Homestead exemptions. Any person the age of eighteen or over, married or single, may hold as a homestead exempt from attachment, execution and forced sale, not exceeding $400,000 in value, any one of the following: The person's interest in real property in one compact body upon which exists a dwelling house in which the person resides; The person's interest in one condominium or cooperative in which the person resides; A mobile home in which the person resides; A mobile home in which the person resides plus the land upon which that mobile home is located.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1101(B)
Only one homestead exemption may be held by a married couple or a single person under this section. The value as specified in this section refers to the equity of a single person or married couple. If a married couple lived together in a dwelling house, a condominium or cooperative, a mobile home or a mobile home plus land on which the mobile home is located and are then divorced, the total exemption allowed for that residence to either or both persons shall not exceed $400,000 in value.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1101(C)
The homestead exemption, not exceeding the value provided for in subsection A, automatically attaches to the person's interest in identifiable cash proceeds from the voluntary or involuntary sale of the property. The homestead exemption in identifiable cash proceeds continues for eighteen months after the date of the sale of the property or until the person establishes a new homestead with the proceeds, whichever period is shorter. Only one homestead exemption at a time may be held by a person under this section.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1121
Availability of exemptions. In the case of married persons, each spouse is entitled to the exemptions provided in this article, which may be combined with the other spouse's exemption in the same property or taken in different exempt property.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1123
Household furniture, furnishings and appliances. Household furniture and furnishings, household goods, including consumer electronic devices, and household appliances personally used by the debtor or a dependent of the debtor and not otherwise specifically prescribed in this chapter are exempt from process provided their aggregate fair market value does not exceed $15,000.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1125
Personal items. The following property of a debtor used primarily for personal, family or household purposes is exempt from process:

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1125(1)
All wearing apparel of not more than a fair market value of five hundred dollars.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1125(2)
All musical instruments provided for the debtor's individual or family use of not more than an aggregate fair market value of four hundred dollars.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1125(3)
Horses, milk cows and poultry of not more than an aggregate fair market value of one thousand dollars.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1125(4)
All engagement and wedding rings of not more than an aggregate fair market value of two thousand dollars.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1125(5)
The library of a debtor, including books, manuals, published materials and personal documents of not more than an aggregate fair market value of two hundred fifty dollars.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1125(6)
One watch of not more than a fair market value of two hundred fifty dollars.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1125(8)
Equity in one motor vehicle of not more than $15,000.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1125(9)
Professionally prescribed prostheses for the debtor or a dependent of the debtor, including a wheelchair or motorized mobility device.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1125(10)
All firearms of not more than an aggregate fair market value of two thousand dollars.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1125(11)
All domestic animals or household pets.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1126(A)
Money benefits or proceeds. The following property of a debtor is exempt from execution, attachment or sale on any process issued from any court:

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1126(A)(9)
A total of $5,000 held in a single account in any one financial institution.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1130
Tools and equipment used in a commercial activity, trade, business or profession. The following tools and equipment of a debtor used in a commercial activity, trade, business or profession shall be exempt from process:

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1130(1)
The tools, equipment, instruments and books, including telephone numbers, client or customer contact information, or marketing tools, such as websites, domain names or any other intangible work product, in the possession of a debtor or the spouse of a debtor primarily used in, and necessary to carry on or develop, the commercial activity, trade, business or profession of the debtor or the debtor's spouse, not in excess of an aggregate fair market value of five thousand dollars. For the purpose of this paragraph, tools do not include a motor vehicle primarily used by a debtor for personal, family or household purposes such as transportation to and from the debtor's place of employment.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1130(2)
Farm machinery, utensils, implements of husbandry, feed, seed, grain and animals not in excess of an aggregate value of two thousand five hundred dollars.

Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1133(B)
In accordance with 11 U.S.C. 522 (b), residents of this state are not entitled to the federal exemptions provided in 11 U.S.C. 522 (d).

Illinois Compiled Statutes
735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-901
Sec. 12-901. Amount. Every individual is entitled to an estate of homestead to the extent in value of $15,000 of his or her interest in a farm or lot of land and buildings thereon, a condominium, or personal property, owned or rightly possessed by lease or otherwise and occupied by him or her as a residence, or in a cooperative that owns property that the individual uses as a residence. That homestead and all right in and title to that homestead is exempt from attachment, judgment, levy, or judgment sale for the payment of his or her debts or other purposes and from the laws of conveyance, descent, and legacy. This Section is not applicable between joint tenants or tenants in common but it is applicable as to any creditors of those persons. If 2 or more individuals own property that is exempt as a homestead, the value of the exemption of each individual may not exceed his or her proportionate share of $30,000 based upon percentage of ownership.

735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-906
Sec. 12-906. Proceeds of sale. When a homestead is conveyed by the owner thereof, such conveyance shall not subject the premises to any lien or incumbrance to which it would not be subject in the possession of such owner; and the proceeds thereof, to the extent of the amount of $15,000, shall be exempt from judgment or other process, for one year after the receipt thereof, by the person entitled to the exemption, and if reinvested in a homestead the same shall be entitled to the same exemption as the original homestead.

735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001
Sec. 12-1001. Personal property exempt. The following personal property, owned by the debtor, is exempt from judgment, attachment, or distress for rent:

735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(a)
The necessary wearing apparel, bible, school books, and family pictures of the debtor and the debtor's dependents;

735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b)
The debtor's equity interest, not to exceed $4,000 in value, in any other property;

735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(c)
The debtor's interest, not to exceed $2,400 in value, in any one motor vehicle;

735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(d)
The debtor's equity interest, not to exceed $1,500 in value, in any implements, professional books, or tools of the trade of the debtor;

735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(e)
Professionally prescribed health aids for the debtor or a dependent of the debtor;

735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001
The personal property exemptions set forth in this Section shall apply only to individuals and only to personal property that is used for personal rather than business purposes.

735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1201
Sec. 12-1201. Bankruptcy exemption. In accordance with the provision of Section 522(b) of the Bankruptcy Code of 1978, (11 U.S.C. 522(b)), residents of this State shall be prohibited from using the federal exemptions provided in Section 522(d) of the Bankruptcy Code of 1978 (11 U.S.C. 522(d)).

Oregon Revised Statutes
Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)
Exempt personal property generally. All property, including franchises, or rights or interest therein, of the judgment debtor, shall be liable to an execution, except as provided in this section. The following property, or rights or interest therein of the judgment debtor, shall be exempt from execution:

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(a)
Books, pictures and musical instruments to the value of $600.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(b)
Wearing apparel and jewelry to the value of $1,800.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(c)
The tools, implements, apparatus, team, harness or library, necessary to enable the judgment debtor to carry on the trade, occupation or profession by which the judgment debtor habitually earns a living, to the value of $5,000.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(d)
A vehicle to the value of $3,000. As used in this paragraph “vehicle” includes an automobile, truck, trailer, truck and trailer or other motor vehicle.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(e)
Domestic animals and poultry kept for family use, to the total value of $1,000 and food sufficient to support such animals and poultry for 60 days.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(f)
Household goods, furniture, radios, a television set and utensils all to the total value of $3,000, if the judgment debtor holds the property primarily for the personal, family or household use of the judgment debtor; provisions actually provided for family use and necessary for the support of a householder and family for 60 days and also 60 days' supply of fuel.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(h)
All professionally prescribed health aids for the debtor or a dependent of the debtor.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(p)
The debtor's interest, not to exceed $400 in value, in any personal property.

Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(3)
If two or more members of a household are joint judgment debtors, each judgment debtor shall be entitled to claim the exemptions in subsection (1)(a), (b), (c), (d) and (p) of this section in the same or different properties. Homestead exemption. The exemption shall be effective without the necessity of a claim thereof by the judgment debtor. When two or more members of a household are debtors whose interests in the homestead are subject to sale on execution, the lien of a judgment or liability in any form, their combined exemptions under this section shall not exceed $50,000. The homestead must be the actual abode of and occupied by the owner, or the owner's spouse, parent or child, but the exemption shall not be impaired by: Temporary removal or temporary absence with the intention to reoccupy the same as a homestead; (b) Removal or absence from the property; or The sale of the property.
